lines.en: Hey Isla! **Do you want to** spend Saturday together?
lines.pt: Ei, Isla! Você quer passar o sábado comigo?

lines.en: **Let’s meet** at ten in the park. We can play soccer.
lines.pt: Vamos nos encontrar às dez no parque. Podemos jogar futebol.

lines.en: **Two tickets for** the movie at seven? I’ll buy them.
lines.pt: Dois ingressos para o filme das sete? Eu compro.

lines.en: Perfect! **I’ll bring** snacks. And my camera.
lines.pt: Perfeito! Eu levo lanches. E a minha câmera.
Legal! Me manda as fotos depois.

lines.en: Sure. **BTW**, should I bring a jacket?
lines.pt: Claro. A propósito, devo levar um casaco?

lines.en: Yes, it gets cold at night.

pages.title: Mission Day: A Free Saturday
pages.pt: Missão da unidade 7: um sábado livre

situation.text: It is Saturday and you are free. You invite a friend, plan the day, get movie tickets, go to a party, share photos and message a new friend: one day, six real situations.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can chain six situations from the unit: talk about hobbies, invite and plan, buy tickets, go to a party, send messages and meet someone online.
canDo: Invite a friend and plan a day
Buy tickets and give an opinion
Go to a party and leave politely
Message friends and stay safe online
pages.think: If you have a free Saturday, which parts of this unit would you use first?

teach.goal: Abrir a aula pela situação real, não pela regra.
solo: Leia o objetivo em voz alta e peça que o estudante diga, com as próprias palavras, o que vai conseguir fazer hoje.
Faça a pergunta “Think about it” antes de mostrar qualquer expressão.
group: Cada estudante diz UMA palavra que associa à situação de hoje.
Mostre os critérios de sucesso: eles são a missão final da aula.
extra: What would be your perfect Saturday?
What movie do you want to see?
support: Aceite respostas curtas ou em português na primeira rodada e reformule em inglês.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Start with real questions about the student’s life, not a grammar test.
intro.group: One question per student, then a question back to a classmate.

pages.recall: Unit 7 review: I like to… · Do you want to…? · Two tickets for… · Can I bring…? · Send me the… · Where are you from?

qs.q: What do you usually do on Saturdays?
qs.pt: O que você costuma fazer aos sábados?

qs.q: Which class in this unit did you like the most?
qs.pt: De qual aula desta unidade você mais gostou?

qs.q: What is one new expression you use now?
qs.pt: Qual expressão nova você usa agora?

pages.tip: Use the answers to find gaps and to recycle earlier content. The goal is to enter English from the first minute.

teach.goal: Entrar no idioma no primeiro minuto e retomar a aula anterior.
extra: Who do you invite first?
Which hobby do you want to try?

errors.r: Do you want to play soccer?

support: Ofereça as respostas-modelo (chips) e peça apenas que escolham uma.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — A free Saturday in the USA
pages.intro: A free Saturday in the USA can mix many things: a sport in the park, a movie, a party and chats with friends. Look and guess before you read.

cards.note: Many parks have fields and courts where people play for free.
Plans are often made by text, and tickets are usually bought online or at the box office.
Guests often bring a dish. It is polite to ask the host first.

qs.q: How do friends make plans in the USA?
qs.pt: Como amigos fazem planos nos EUA?

levels.A2: They text or use a group chat.
levels.B1: Plans are often made by text, then confirmed the same day.
levels.B2: Short messages make a plan flexible: people suggest a time, a place and adjust until it works.

qs.q: What helps conversation in a new place?
qs.pt: O que ajuda a conversar em um lugar novo?

levels.A2: Easy questions like “Where are you from?”.
levels.B1: Simple questions about hobbies and plans start a friendly chat.
levels.B2: Light topics such as hobbies, teams and plans make it easy to connect without being too personal.

qs.q: Why is politeness important in all these situations?
qs.pt: Por que a educação é importante em todas essas situações?

levels.B1: Please, thanks and a short reason make requests and goodbyes sound friendly.
levels.B2: Small words like please and thanks, plus a short reason to leave or decline, keep every interaction smooth.

pages.compare: In Brazil a free Saturday often means friends, food and music too. Which situation from this unit would you use most on your Saturday?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural e as primeiras hipóteses.
solo: Mostre os 3 cartões e peça hipóteses antes de explicar.
Peça que o estudante compare com o que acontece no Brasil.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica em uma frase.
Pergunte “Do you agree?” entre colegas.
answers: Q1: mensagens e grupos de conversa.
Q2: perguntas simples sobre hobbies e planos.
Q3: please, thanks e um motivo curto.
extra: What do you bring to a party?
What do you text your friends?
support: Use as respostas do nível A1 como andaime e peça que repitam.
stretch: B2: compare as convenções sociais do Brasil e dos EUA nessa situação.

teach.goal: Compreender a situação antes de ver o texto: ideia principal e depois informações específicas.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: só a ideia principal.
2ª escuta: as informações da lista.
Mostre o texto só depois da 2ª escuta.
group: Escuta coletiva; duplas anotam as respostas antes de revelar.
Compare as respostas entre as duplas e só então mostre o texto.
extra: Who is speaking? How do you know?
What movie do you want to see?
support: Pause depois de cada fala se necessário.

retell.prompt: Retell the conversation in your own words, at your level.

teach.goal: Ler o diálogo, perceber os chunks e recontar.
solo: O estudante lê um papel; você lê o outro. Depois troquem.
Peça que reconte a conversa no nível que conseguir.
group: Leitura em duplas e troca de papéis.
Reconto em cadeia: uma frase por estudante.
answers: The park at ten · soccer · the movie at seven · snacks and a camera
extra: Which hobby do you want to try?
What was your favorite class in this unit?
support: Mostre a tradução (botão PT) depois da 2ª leitura.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.use: Fix a time and a place (class 50).
Ask for a link or photo (class 54).

items.en: Do you want to watch the game?
Two tickets for the nine o’clock show.

pages.note: Instead of memorizing the whole list, choose 3–5 expressions (★) to use again and again. The others are for understanding and for stretching later.

teach.goal: Escolher 3–5 chunks para uso repetido e descobrir a função de cada um.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?” antes de dar o significado.
Compare formal × informal e peça um exemplo próprio.
group: Cada estudante escolhe a expressão que mais usaria e explica quando.
Compare equivalentes formais e informais em duplas.
answers: Inviting · Fixing time and place · Buying tickets · Asking for something · Meeting someone
extra: What do you text your friends?
What would be your perfect Saturday?
support: Trabalhe só as 3 expressões ★ nesta aula.

patterns.name: Inviting and planning
ex: Do you want to play soccer?

patterns.name: Buying and asking
patterns.formula: **Two tickets for** + movie  /  **Send me the** + noun
ex: Two tickets for the seven o’clock show.

patterns.name: Meeting people
patterns.formula: **Where are you from?**  /  **What do you do for fun?**
ex: What do you do for fun?

swap.frame: Do you want to {do} {when}? I’ll bring {thing}.

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: Would you like to join us?
Could you please send me the photos?
By the way, please bring a jacket.
register.note: These are differences of context and register, not absolute rules: contractions and short forms also appear in informal writing.

teach.goal: Fixar os 2 padrões principais; os outros são expansão. Usar a troca de palavras para variar a fala.
solo: Mostre o padrão DENTRO do diálogo (grife os chunks).
Use “Swap the words”: toque em cada peça e peça a frase completa.
Compare spoken × written em 2 exemplos.
group: Troca em cadeia: cada estudante muda UMA peça e o próximo repete a frase.
Em pares: um escolhe as peças, o outro fala.
teach.answers: Os padrões 01 e 02 são o foco; os demais são expansão para quem avançar rápido.
extra: What do you never share online?
Who do you invite first?
support: Fique só com o primeiro padrão na primeira rodada.
stretch: Combinar dois padrões na mesma frase.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: Review of the unit: the important words are strong and the small words are weak. “Do you WANT to PLAY SOCcer?” Say the plan with this rhythm.

items.say: Two tickets for the seven o’clock show.
items.linked: Two TICK-ets for the SEV-en o’CLOCK SHOW.
items.ipa: /ˈtu ˈtɪkəts fər ðə ˈsɛvən əˈklɑk ˈʃoʊ/

own.prompt: Write a sentence about your Saturday plan.
own.criteria: Say it twice. Did the important words sound stronger than the small words?

solo: 3 passagens: escutar e identificar → reproduzir ritmo e entonação → usar em frase com conteúdo próprio.
Modele devagar e normal; peça que o estudante bata palmas na sílaba forte.
group: Coro, depois duplas; circule ouvindo.
Cada estudante cria uma frase própria.
answers: Identify: Let’s meet at ten. · Send me the photos.

errors.r: Do you want to play soccer?

support: Reduza a velocidade e conte as batidas em voz alta.

levels.h: Controlled practice — choose the best answer

items.q: 1. You want to invite a friend to play soccer.
opts: Do you want to play soccer?

items.q: 2. You want to buy movie tickets.
opts: Two tickets for the seven o’clock show, please.
items.why: Two tickets for + show, with please.

items.q: 3. You go to a party and you want to bring something.
4. You meet a new friend online.

levels.h: Guided practice — complete, substitute and transform

ans: Could you send me the photos?
Could you send me the photos, please?
items.model: Could you send me the photos?
items.why: Could you + base verb is polite.

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado: completar, substituir e transformar antes da fala livre.
solo: Peça que o estudante justifique cada resposta.
Se acertar rápido, peça a versão mais informal ou mais educada.
group: Resolvam em duplas e comparem antes de revelar.
Equipes: ponto por resposta justificada.
answers: 1: Do you want to play soccer? · 2: Two tickets for the seven o’clock show, please. · 3: Can I bring dessert? · 4: Where are you from?
Gap: meet · better · Could you send me the photos? · I’m into music. · Yes! It was great.
extra: What was your favorite class in this unit?
What do you bring to a party?
support: Ofereça o banco de palavras (chips) nas lacunas.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — a free Saturday

brief.teacher: You are the friend who changes plans during the day (change the plan during the scene!).
brief.student: You are the main person: invite, plan, buy tickets, go to a party and message a friend.

orders: Plan a Saturday with soccer and a movie
Plan a Saturday with a concert and a party
Plan a Saturday with a hobby, a movie and a message
complications: The movie you want is sold out: choose another show.
Your friend can’t come at ten: suggest a new time.
At the party you don’t know anyone: start a conversation.
A new online friend asks for your address: refuse politely.

teach.goal: Simulação com complicação inesperada e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Ligue o cenário à vida do estudante.
Rodada 1: com chunks. Rodada 2: só palavras-chave. Rodada 3: sem roteiro.
Meta de fala: 60–70% do tempo para o estudante. Anote 2–3 correções para a devolutiva.
extra: What would be your perfect Saturday?
What movie do you want to see?
support: Volte à rodada 1 se travar; peça que repita só a primeira frase.
stretch: Peça que o estudante conte o sábado inteiro, do convite à despedida.

rounds.title: Invite and plan
rounds.task: Station 1: invite your partner and fix a time and place.
rounds.hint: Do you want to…? / Let’s meet at…

rounds.title: Movie and snacks
rounds.task: Station 2: buy tickets and ask the show time.
rounds.hint: Two tickets for… / What time is the show?

rounds.title: Party and chat
rounds.task: Station 3: arrive at a party, ask to bring something, meet a new person.
rounds.hint: Can I bring…? / Where are you from?

rounds.title: Our Saturday
rounds.task: Whole group: each pair shares the best Saturday plan.

infogap.title: Saturday plan
infogap.instr: Ask your partner and complete your card. Do not look at the other card!

a.title: Student A has Paul’s plan
a.task: You know the morning and the evening. Ask about the afternoon and the night.

b.title: Student B has Isla’s plan
b.task: You know the afternoon and the night. Ask about the morning and the evening.

teach.goal: Fluência por repetição da função com informações novas a cada rodada.
group: Troque os pares a cada rodada (A+B / C+D → A+C / B+D → A+D / B+C → grupo todo). Com 6 estudantes, três duplas simultâneas.
Sem salas simultâneas: interações sequenciais enquanto uma dupla apresenta.
Responsabilidade individual: cada aluno faz ≥1 pergunta e ≥1 resposta.
answers: A tem 10:00 (soccer) e 7:00 (movie); B tem 2:00 (lunch with Beto) e 10:00 (party at Finn’s). Cada um pergunta “What do you do at…?”.
extra: Who do you invite first?
Which hobby do you want to try?
support: Entregue frases-modelo no chat da turma.

pages.title: Group mission — a free Saturday
pages.goal: Each group must chain at least four situations from the unit in one story: invite, plan, buy tickets or go to a party, share and react.

missions.mission: Talk about hobbies, invite a friend to play, plan a time and a place, and choose snacks.
missions.constraint: Use “I’m into…”, “Do you want to…?” and “Let’s meet at…”.
missions.start: Hey! What do you do in your free time?

missions.mission: Buy two movie tickets, choose a time, order popcorn and say if you liked the movie.
missions.constraint: Use “Two tickets for…”, “What time is the show?” and “Did you like it?”.

missions.mission: Go to a party, offer to bring something, send photos by text and meet a new friend online.
missions.constraint: Use “Can I bring…?”, “Send me the…” and “Where are you from?”.

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: o objetivo é resolver, não só falar certo.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão. Alterne os papéis.
Progressão: 1ª rodada com frases de apoio, 2ª só palavras-chave, 3ª sem roteiro.
Observe e anote 2–3 correções prioritárias; devolutiva no fim.
answers: “Do you want to play soccer?” → “Sure! Let’s meet at ten.” → “Two tickets for the seven o’clock show, please.” → “Can I bring snacks?” → “Send me the photos.”
extra: What do you bring to a party?
What do you text your friends?
support: Dê o início de frase (“Start with”) em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a message to a friend with your plan for a free Saturday. Invite, plan, ask for something and say goodbye.
pages.model: Hi Isla! **Do you want to** spend Saturday together? **Let’s meet** at ten in the park. After that, **two tickets for** the seven o’clock movie? **Send me the** photos later, please. See you!
checklist: I gave a time and a place.
I asked for something and said goodbye.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea instead of rewriting everything.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação comunicativa.
solo: Peça o texto; corrija 2–3 pontos prioritários e mostre uma forma mais natural.
group: Cada estudante escreve; depois troquem os textos entre colegas e corrijam em duplas.
extra: What movie do you want to see?
What do you never share online?

errors.r: Do you want to play soccer?

support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.desc: Mantém a comunicação sem interrupções excessivas.

criteria.name: Language use
criteria.desc: Utiliza adequadamente padrões, vocabulário e expressões.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.desc: É compreensível e usa ritmo e entonação adequados.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Raise complexity and speed; add follow-up questions.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

prompts.well: Example: You invited, planned and solved a small problem with confidence.
prompts.improve: Example: Put the strong stress on the important words in your plan.
prompts.next: Example: Tell the whole Saturday story in one minute without notes.

teach.goal: Avaliar o que o aluno conseguiu comunicar, não só os erros gramaticais.
solo: O estudante se autoavalia primeiro; depois você.
Feche com os três blocos: What you did well · What to improve · Your next challenge.
group: Dê um comentário por critério a cada estudante.
Cada um escolhe o próprio próximo desafio.
teach.answers: A rubrica é uma ferramenta interna de acompanhamento, não uma certificação CEFR.

tasks.name: Build a question
tasks.prompt: Without notes: invite a friend to see a movie.
tasks.model: Do you want to see a movie?

tasks.name: Respond to a situation
tasks.prompt: A friend says: “Let’s meet at ten.” You agree.

tasks.name: Use a new expression
tasks.prompt: Say you have to leave a party politely.
tasks.model: I’d better go. Thanks for having me!

items: Record a 60-second audio telling your free Saturday plan.
Write a short message inviting a friend to your plan.
Review three expressions from the unit and create your own examples.
Listen to the dialogue again and identify two expressions.

teach.goal: Toda aula termina com uma produção observável.
solo: Sem consultar as anotações: construir uma pergunta, responder a uma situação e usar uma expressão nova.
group: Exit challenge individual; compare com o colega e combine a tarefa de continuidade.
answers: Do you want to see a movie? · Sounds good! · I’d better go. Thanks for having me!
extra: Revisão espaçada: retomar na próxima aula, depois de uma semana e na missão de encerramento da unidade.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.goal: Suggest a plan with short phrases.

ladder.say: Do you want to play soccer on Saturday? Let’s meet at ten.
I thought we could play soccer in the morning and catch a movie afterwards, if you’re up for it.
How about we start with a game in the park and see where the day takes us from there?
I’d suggest keeping the day loose: a kickabout in the morning, then we can play the rest by ear.
Let’s leave the afternoon open and let the day shape itself.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
